exercises.name: Easy Walk
exercises.note: READ THIS ONCE BEFORE YOU START. This session is for ordinary, mechanical back pain that a doctor or physio has already looked at and cleared you to train through. It is not a diagnosis and it is not treatment. Stop and get it looked at properly if you have pain running down your leg, numbness, pins and needles, weakness in a leg or foot, any change in bladder or bowel control, pain that started after a fall, pain that wakes you at night, or pain with feeling unwell. Those are not things to train through. And on any exercise here: an ache you can breathe through is fine, a sharp pain is not. If something bites, stop that one and tell me.

good: Walk before anything else. It is the single most useful thing for a sore back
Easy pace, tall posture, let the arms swing
Outside is better than a treadmill if you have the option
bad: Skipping it to get to the exercises. This is the exercise

exercises.name: Glute Bridge
exercises.note: Your glutes are the engine that should move your hips. When they are asleep, your lower back does their job for them, and it does it badly. Two minutes here changes what the rest of the session feels like.

good: Ribs down, squeeze the glutes and lift until your hips are level. No higher
Pause a second at the top of each one and feel the glute, not the lower back
bad: Arching the back to lift higher. Height is not the point
Feeling this in your hamstrings or your back. Move your feet closer if so

exercises.name: Half-Kneeling Hip Flexor with Overhead Reach
exercises.note: Here is the whole idea of this block. Your lower back is not stiff so much as it is doing the moving for joints that will not. Free up the hips and the upper back, keep the lower back still and strong, and it stops being asked to do a job it was never built for. That is why nothing in this session stretches your lower back itself.

good: Half-kneeling, squeeze the back glute first, then reach the same-side arm overhead
Tuck the tailbone under and keep the ribs down before you reach
You should feel it at the front of the back hip, never in your lower back
bad: Arching the lower back to feel more. That is the opposite of the point
Pushing the hips forward without the glute squeeze

good: Both knees bent at ninety, rotate them slowly to the other side
Sit tall. Put your hands behind you for support if you need to
Go only as far as you can control, and no further
bad: Forcing the knees down with your hands
Rounding your back to get further round

good: On your side, knees stacked and together, open the top arm and follow it with your eyes
The knees staying together is what makes the turn happen in your ribs
Breathe out as you open
bad: Letting the top knee lift, which just moves the rotation into your lower back

good: On your back, ankle across the opposite knee, pull the bottom thigh towards you
Head and shoulders stay down on the floor
A tight glute is one of the most common reasons a back stays sore
bad: Pulling hard enough that your hips lift off the floor
Curling your head and shoulders up to reach

exercises.name: Modified Curl-Up
exercises.note: Three things make this different from a sit-up, and all three matter. Your hands go UNDER your lower back to hold its natural arch, so the spine never flexes. One knee stays bent and one leg stays straight, which locks the pelvis. And you lift barely an inch, head and shoulders together like they are glued. If your lower back flattens into the floor, you are doing a sit-up. Also: leave this one alone for the first hour after you wake up, when the discs are most swollen and least happy about being bent.

good: Hands palm-down under the small of your back. Do not let that arch flatten
One knee bent, one leg straight. Swap legs between sets
Lift head and shoulders barely an inch and hold for ten. Breathe through the hold
Descending sets, so it gets easier as you tire. Never to failure
bad: Pulling your chin to your chest or lacing your hands behind your head
Lifting high. An inch is the whole range
Holding your breath

exercises.name: Side Bridge
exercises.note: Start on your knees. Everyone wants to start from the feet and most people should not. Move to the feet version only when you can hold the knee version for ten seconds with your hips perfectly stacked and no sag, on both sides, for every rep of every set. Your weaker side decides the progression, not your stronger one.

good: On your side, elbow under the shoulder, knees bent and stacked
Lift the hips into a straight line and hold ten seconds, then lower under control
Hips stacked one on top of the other, never rolled forward
bad: Letting the hips sag or the top hip roll towards the floor
Going to the straight-leg version before the knee version is easy

exercises.name: Bird Dog
exercises.note: The last of the three, and the one everyone rushes. Long and slow beats high and fast every time. If someone put a glass of water on your lower back, it should not spill once in the whole set. Sweeping the hand and foot back to the middle between reps, rather than resting them down, is what keeps the trunk working.

good: Opposite arm and leg, reach long rather than lift high, back flat
Hold ten seconds, then sweep the elbow and knee towards each other and straight back out
Hips stay square to the floor the whole time
bad: Lifting the leg above hip height and arching the back
Letting the hips twist open towards the lifting leg
Rushing, so the trunk never has to hold anything

exercises.name: Supine Rest, Calves Elevated
exercises.note: You will notice there is no foam rolling here and nothing that stretches the lower back. That is deliberate. A sore lower back does not want to be pressed on or pulled into end range, and the classic knees-to-chest stretch is the one that makes a lot of backs worse the next morning. What it does want is to be unloaded and to stop guarding. That is what these last four minutes are.

good: On your back, calves resting on a chair or a sofa, knees at about ninety
Arms out wide, palms up. Nothing to hold
This takes the load off the lower back completely. Let it be heavy
bad: Pulling your knees to your chest instead. Not in this session

exercises.name: Extended Exhale Breathing
exercises.note: A back that hurts is usually a back that is bracing all day without being asked to. Long, slow out-breaths are the fastest way to tell everything around it to let go. Stay in the same position and just change the breathing. If this suits you, there is a whole Breath section in the Library.

good: In through the nose for four, out for eight
One hand on the belly. Only that hand should move
Let the shoulders and the jaw go on every exhale
bad: Forcing big breaths
Getting straight up when the timer goes. Take a few normal breaths first
